sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Tempe, AZ?
sections.html:
You have three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an offer from a cash buyer who purchases as-is. In Maricopa County all three finish the same way, with a signed contract, an escrow at a title company, a deed recorded with the county and a sales affidavit filed alongside it.

The route sets your timeline. A listing reaches the widest group of buyers, but you handle showings, repairs and the buyer's financing and inspection periods. An as-is cash sale usually gives up some price in return for fewer steps and a closing date you choose. Tempe is a city where renters outnumber owners, so many sellers here are landlords, heirs or owners of a house that has sat vacant, and those situations add their own paperwork.

Before you contact anyone, gather these items:

  • A payoff figure from every lender or lienholder on the house.
  • The Maricopa County Assessor parcel number, which the sales affidavit asks for.
  • Permit records for any addition, patio cover or garage conversion.
  • Current leases and the rental registration details if tenants live there.
  • Your 2026 property tax statement from the Maricopa County Treasurer.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Tempe homes?
sections.html:
Tempe is a high-value, renter-heavy city. The Census Bureau estimates 190,571 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 3.5% from the April 2020 estimates base, and reports an owner-occupied housing rate of 42.3% for 2020 to 2024.

These are citywide midpoints. A 1960s ranch near Tempe Town Lake and a townhome south of US 60 can sit far from the median, so price your own house from recent sales on its street. The same table shows 2.27 people per household, 50.0% of adults 25 and older holding a bachelor's degree and an average commute of 20.9 minutes.

sections.h2: What is Tempe like, and how does the layout affect a sale?
sections.html:
Tempe is an inner suburb of Phoenix with about 39.94 square miles of land. Mesa is on the east, Scottsdale and the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community on the north, Phoenix and Guadalupe on the west, and Chandler on the south. The Salt River runs through the north end, and two dams there form Tempe Town Lake.

Development is dense in the north around Arizona State University and the Valley Metro light rail line, then thins to single-family streets, strip centers and low-rise office parks toward the south. The terrain is flat apart from Hayden Butte, known as A-Mountain, beside the university.

The area was farmed by the Hohokam, who dug canals there. Settlers later ran a ferry on the river, and Darrell Duppa suggested the name Tempe in 1879. The territorial legislature chose the town for a normal school in 1885, which grew into ASU, and a railroad bridge across the Salt River followed in 1887. The city's 2020 financial report lists ASU and State Farm Insurance as its two largest employers.

Buyers ask about commutes first, so lead with these:

  • Interstate 10 touches the western edge, Loop 202 crosses the north, Loop 101 follows the eastern border and US 60 runs east to west through the middle.
  • Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport sits about 2 miles northwest.
  • Valley Metro Rail serves Downtown Tempe and ASU, and the city runs free Orbit shuttle routes near the campus.

Most of Tempe is in the Tempe Elementary School District and the Tempe Union High School District. Parts are served by the Kyrene School District (K to 8), Scottsdale Unified and Mesa Public Schools, so confirm the district for your address before you put it in a listing.

sections.h2: How does Tempe's desert heat affect the house I am selling?
sections.html:
The heat makes the cooling system the item buyers care about most. Tempe has a hot-desert climate, with average daily highs of 103.7 degrees in June, 105.9 in July and 104.8 in August, and a recorded high of 119. Yearly precipitation averages 8.80 inches.

A cooling unit that struggles in July is a bargaining point, and an old evaporative cooler or a roof with sun-cracked coating invites a repair credit request. If the unit is near the end of its life, get a written quote before you list so the number is yours and not the buyer's.

Rare storms do happen. An F2 tornado crossed Tempe on August 30, 1971 and injured 41 people. Check roof and window condition after any storm and keep the repair paperwork with your disclosure records.

sections.h2: Do I need permits or repairs before selling in Tempe?
sections.html:
Any work you did on the house should have its permits closed out before you list. The city's Building Safety Division is at 31 East 5th Street, Garden Level East, east of Mill Avenue between 5th and 6th Streets. Reach the permit center at PermitCenter@tempe.gov or 480-350-4311.

Residential plan review covers single-family homes, duplexes and townhomes. New construction, additions, renovations, remodels and accessory structures need plan approval before a permit is issued. The same staff answer accessory dwelling unit questions.

If a previous owner added a room, a carport or a casita, ask the division what is on record for your address. Learning that before a buyer's agent asks gives you time to finish or close a permit instead of negotiating around it.

sections.h2: What rules apply if my Tempe house is a rental or short-term rental?
sections.html:
Every rental in Tempe must be registered with the Maricopa County Assessor's Office, and rentals of fewer than 30 days also need a city license. Check both before you sell a rented or recently rented house.

Tempe's rental housing code sets standards that an inspecting buyer may notice. Landlords must provide:

  • Heating under the tenant's control that can bring habitable rooms to at least 70 degrees.
  • Cooling that holds rooms at 82 degrees or less with air conditioning, or 88 degrees or less with evaporative cooling.
  • Hot water at a minimum of 110 degrees.
  • Landscaping in yard areas visible to the public.

For short-term rentals, anyone renting a property for 29 days or less needs a Tempe Short-Term Rental License, one per unit. The annual fee is $250, or $187.50 if issued after July 1, and licenses expire each January 1. Operating without one can bring a penalty of up to $1,000 per month. Owners must show $500,000 or more in liability coverage, notify adjacent neighbors and carry a state transaction privilege tax license. Questions go to Tempe Tax and License at 480-350-2955 or license@tempe.gov, including whether a license on the property stays with it after a sale.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when I sell in Tempe?
sections.html:
Maricopa County bills and collects the tax on a Tempe house, not the city. Tax statements arrive in two installments, and the county's calendar shows 2026 first-half taxes were due October 1 and became delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 2, 2026. That date has passed, so confirm with the Treasurer whether yours is paid.

December 31, 2026 is the last day to pay current full-year taxes without interest on bills over $100. Under A.R.S. 42-18052 the second installment is due March 1 and becomes delinquent after May 1. On a closing, the escrow officer normally pays what is owed from your proceeds, so ask the title company to request a payoff from the Treasurer.

If you think the assessed value of your house is wrong, the Arizona Department of Revenue says a real property appeal goes to the County Assessor within 60 days of the Notice of Value. Appeals are about value and classification, and a high tax bill by itself is not a ground.

sections.h2: What are the deed and recording steps for a Tempe house?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder at 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200, Phoenix, open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The standard recording fee is $30 per document, with some exceptions, and documents can be recorded in person, by mail or electronically.

Arizona law requires an Affidavit of Property Value with each deed, unless the transfer is exempt and the deed carries an exemption code. Under A.R.S. 11-1133 the buyer and seller, or their agents, certify the sale date, total price, financing type, parcel number and whether the house will be owner-occupied or rented. The recorder must refuse a deed that lacks a complete affidavit. The state notes that the sale date is the date the contract was signed, not the closing date. Your title company prepares and files this package, but read the affidavit before you sign it.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Tempe house for a weekend or a week?
faqs.a: Yes. Tempe requires a Short-Term Rental License for rentals of 29 days or less, one license per unit, and you must apply before you list. The fee is $250 a year, or $187.50 if issued after July 1, and the license expires January 1.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to on a Tempe house?
faqs.a: You pay the Maricopa County Treasurer, not the City of Tempe. The Arizona Department of Revenue says tax bills are paid to the County Treasurer, usually in two installments due October 1 and March 1.

faqs.q: What form does Arizona require to record a deed in Tempe?
faqs.a: An Affidavit of Property Value, which is ADOR Form 82162, unless the transfer is exempt. An exempt deed carries the statute and exemption code on its face. The Maricopa County Recorder will not accept a deed with a missing or incomplete affidavit.

faqs.q: Where can I get permit records for my Tempe address?
faqs.a: Contact the Building Safety Division at PermitCenter@tempe.gov or 480-350-4311. Staff can tell you what permits are on file, which matters if a prior owner built an addition or accessory structure.

faqs.q: What if I have not paid the first half of my 2026 Tempe property tax?
faqs.a: Pay it or ask your escrow officer to pay it from the sale. The first half became delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 2, 2026. The county calendar lists December 31 as the last day to pay current full-year taxes without interest.
